sessions.feedback: The economic_calendar tool still showed 08:30 ET releases (PCE, GDP) as "not out yet" about 3-5 minutes after the release time; a feed timestamp or "last updated" field would help. The digest's pre-market list is dominated by thin prints (<1% of average volume), so adding a minimum volume filter would make it more useful. Otherwise nothing blocked a trade this session.

Nothing blocked me. Two small tooling notes: web_search sometimes returns a str that must be JSON-parsed, and the scan tool's 'earnings' column helps but doesn't show beat or miss. A field with the post-earnings surprise (EPS vs consensus) in scan, or a list of today's reporters with surprise and pre-market reaction, would speed up screening for beats that did not gap.

Nothing blocked me this session. Two suggestions. (1) read_page failed on CNBC and Investing.com URLs, so I got the article text from web_search results instead; a note on which domains read_page can fetch would help. (2) A screener-style tool listing the largest idiosyncratic moves (versus industry) across all eligible stocks, including after-hours, would find catalysts faster than the digest's top-20 list, which is dominated by thin pre-market prints (100 to 1,000 shares). Stops and targets are fixed at entry, so I could not tell which stop width suits the volatility; the stop sat 0.7% below the close in a 3%-a-day tape, and I only fixed it through extend.

It is unclear whether a stop that gaps through (NVDA pre-market 141 versus a 144.88 stop) fills at the stop price or at the open price. Documenting that would help me size positions and decide whether to close manually. Otherwise nothing blocked me.

No blockers this session. Suggestions: (1) the digest's pre-market mover list is dominated by thin prints (e.g. OCSL at 200 shares), so a filter on a minimum share count or dollar volume would help. (2) The scan tool's earnings field says 'time not given' for most names, so a before-open/after-close flag would help judge whether a move already includes the earnings reaction (PANW's +9.9% regular-session move looked like earnings but came before the report). (3) A ticker-level 'consensus vs actual' feed would save web searches.

The NVDA CNBC article could not be fetched with read_page. The news tool sometimes labels stories misleadingly: the digest said "SEC investigation" for NVDA, but the cited MarketWatch page did not mention one. The helper answers are useful for checking claims. Reports on GLBE conflicted (+8% vs -12% pre) and cannot be checked from pre-market tools alone. A consensus-vs-actual field in scan would save web searches.

The data was sufficient. Pre-market prints on thin volume (e.g. ESLT +8% on 605 shares, ACM, KNX) are hard to trust, so a pre-market VWAP or a bid/ask indication would help judge the likely opening price. The read_page helper often returns only teasers for paywalled pages, so a way to fetch the SEC exhibit text directly would help. Consensus estimates were not available from the tools and I had to use web search for them.
No blocking issues. A premarket movers list in the digest (not only previous-session movers) would help since orders fill at the open.
No VIX or futures data in tools; would help judge the volatility regime.

summary:
Session 2026-11-25.

Session 2026-11-25 (pre-open, day before Thanksgiving). Context: 11-24 closed SPY -0.49% (718.8), QQQ -1.99% (638), XLK -3.3%, with defensives and consumer up (XLV +2.95%, XLP +1.7%, XLY +0.7%). Pre-market is worse: SPY -1.95% (705), QQQ -2.9% (620, the 11-20 low was ~596), VIXY +9%. Drivers are a WSJ report of sweeping new tariffs on China, the EU and 14 others (announcement possible this week) and AI-hardware multiple compression. PCE was due at 08:30 ET but was not yet in the feed. The Dec 9 Fed hike is ~96% priced.
Portfolio: only AS is open, 7% of equity (cost 30.53, close 30.14, -1.3%, +1.6% on a -2% QQQ day), stop 26.42, target 34.05, horizon 12-08. No company news; pre -1.7% is less than the tape. Held. Cash is 93%, so equity is about -2.1% against SPY about -8% since 10-29.
Examined, no trade: DELL (blowout beat and raise plus $25B buyback, but ISG margin guided down; -11.8% before the print, -5.6% pre, ~9x P/E; AI hardware beats are being sold, HPE -16%); HPQ (FY27 EPS guide in line, weak PCs, mixed); URBN (record Q3 but Anthropologie comps 1.7%, markdowns up, MS downgrade, -12% pre, priced); WDAY/ADSK/NTNX (-4.5%/-5%/-12% pre, priced); AMBA (-34% pre, priced); DE (EPS miss, pre -2.9% in line with the tape); ANT (Anthropic, below its $83 IPO price, $1T cap, no edge); SNY/INSM (priced M&A). The no-chasing rule is mixed: ANF closed +19.7% against pre-market +10.9%, while DKS faded to +14.6% and then flat.
Check next session (11-27 is an early close; 11-26 is closed, so the next session is the 11-27 pre-open): the PCE reaction and QQQ against ~596; tariff announcement details and AS exposure (Asia manufacturing); VIX below ~28; DKS/ANF drift; DELL/HPE for stabilisation; NVDA/Bessent; CRWD 12-01; AS stop 26.42. Redeploy only on stabilisation plus idiosyncratic catalysts, ideally on names that did not gap.

1. Beat-and-raise drift longs fail when macro beta dominates (NVDA, P, ESLT 11-17 to 11-20; ROST/INTU also sold off on beats). Do not add them while QQQ is making new lows; wait for a higher low and falling VIX. In AI hardware, even blowout beats are sold when margins are guided down (DELL, HPE 11-24/25).
2. Honour stops in a rout; do not override (NVDA: the stop saved ~11 more points). But size stops to the vol regime: with SPY moving 3-5%/day an 8-10% stop on a 4-6% daily-vol stock sits inside 2 sigma. AS's stop was widened to 10% on 11-23; AS (3% daily vol, consumer) has held up better than tech.
3. Gap risk: a stop is not a guarantee; NVDA filled -10.0% vs -9.1% stop, P -12.2% vs ~-12% planned.
4. Pre-market strength in a bear tape is not tradable (CRWV 11-11; QQQ +2.1% pre then -2.2% on 11-19). The 11-23 +4.7% rebound faded the next day. Cash is winning versus SPY (equity ~-2.1% vs SPY ~-8% since 10-29), so cash needs a real edge to be replaced.
5. A long beats SPY only with idiosyncratic alpha; a beta bounce bet is a coin flip (about 0.5).
6. Retail earnings include IEEPA tariff-refund benefits - use adjusted numbers (LOW, WSM, TGT, ANF, HPQ).
7. Sympathy gap-ups are not trades. Thin pre-market prints (<1% of avg volume) are unreliable; check shares traded and the IEX last trade.
8. Merger arb: check the spread (ZS vs CRWD ~1.3%; INSM 2.4% for 6 months).
9. No-chasing rule scorecard: ANF closed 11-24 at 168.1 (+19.7%) vs pre-market ~+10.9%, so chasing would have worked on day 1; DKS faded from pre +16.7% to +14.6% close, then flat. Your universe is every eligible US stock. Your style is a few high-quality trades.

- Look for situations where recent, specific information has not yet been reflected in the price:
  earnings surprises and guidance changes, contracts, regulatory decisions, management changes,
  supply problems, sector-wide shocks. Remember you trade at the open, after the overnight reaction,
  so ask what is still left to move, not what already moved. It works in both directions: bad
  news the price has not finished absorbing is a short.
- Prefer clear catalysts you can verify over vague narratives. A strong case beats a busy portfolio,
  so concentrate on your best ideas. Cash is the right answer when thorough research has turned up
  nothing, and only then.
- Size positions by conviction and by how much could go wrong. Set stops and targets you would
  actually stand behind.
- Use the movers and most-active lists as places to start looking, not as reasons to buy.
